name: Petzl Replacement Bridge
title: Petzl Replacement Bridge for Sequoia Saddles
meta: Petzl replacement bridge for Sequoia and Sequoia SRT saddles. When to retire a worn bridge, how to match the right part, and what to check after you install it.
tagline: A factory replacement bridge to put a Petzl Sequoia saddle back in service.
summary: The Petzl replacement bridge lets you swap out a worn or damaged bridge on a Petzl Sequoia or Sequoia SRT saddle instead of retiring the whole harness. It is a wear part, and on a saddle that gets climbed every day it is often the first thing to need replacing.
highlights: Factory replacement bridge from Petzl
For Sequoia and Sequoia SRT tree saddles
Restores the main attachment point without buying a new saddle
Swap it as soon as inspection shows wear
Install per Petzl's instructions
specs: Petzl Sequoia family saddles (confirm model and size)

p: The bridge takes every load you put on the saddle and it slides through a rope-wrench tether, a hitch-climber pulley, or a carabiner hundreds of times a day. Sap, bark grit, and sawdust work into the fibers and act like sandpaper. A bridge that looks fuzzy, glazed, or flat in spots is telling you it is time.
Replacing the bridge is far cheaper than a new harness, and the rest of a Sequoia often has plenty of life left. Keep a spare in the truck so a bad inspection does not end the day.

On a Sequoia the bridge also sets how the saddle sits when you lean back in your lanyard or hang in the climbing line. A bridge that has stretched, been cut, or picked up hard spots changes that feel, and it is a sign the rest of the saddle deserves a close look too.

body.h: Matching the part and checking it
p: Petzl has offered bridges in different lengths and versions over the years, so confirm your saddle model, size, and the bridge length you want before ordering. Other bridges and shoulder harnesses are in saddle parts and shoulder harnesses.

Install it exactly as Petzl's instructions show, then hang-test low and close to the ground before climbing. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.

faq.q: Does the Petzl replacement bridge fit other brands of saddle?
faq.a: It is made for Petzl's own saddles. Do not improvise it onto another brand's harness; use the bridge that manufacturer specifies.

faq.q: How often should I replace a saddle bridge?
faq.a: There is no fixed interval. Replace it whenever inspection shows cuts, heavy abrasion, glazing, or stiff spots, and follow Petzl's lifespan guidance.

name: Yale Fire Replacement Lanyard
title: Yale Fire Replacement Lanyard Rope
meta: Yale Fire replacement lanyard: a fresh rope tail to rebuild a worn positioning lanyard. What to check for length, eye type, and fit with your adjuster.
tagline: A Yale Cordage rope lanyard for rebuilding a worn flipline or positioning lanyard.
summary: The Yale Fire replacement lanyard is a length of Yale Cordage climbing line made to replace the rope in a worn positioning lanyard. You keep your adjuster and snap or carabiner and simply put fresh rope back in service.
highlights: Yale Cordage climbing line, bright and easy to spot
Replaces the rope section of an adjustable lanyard
Keeps your existing adjuster and hardware in use
Cheaper than buying a full new lanyard kit
Check length and end terminations before ordering

body.h: When the rope goes before the hardware
p: A lanyard takes a beating that a climbing line never sees. It gets wrapped around rough bark, pinched in a mechanical adjuster, and nicked by the saw when you are working close. The adjuster and connectors usually outlast the rope by a long way.

Swapping in a replacement lanyard rope keeps a familiar setup on your saddle. A high-visibility line also helps you keep track of where the lanyard sits on the stem while you cut, which is when lanyards get hurt.

Rebuilding a lanyard is also a good moment to rethink length. A climber who spends most of the day on big trunks may want a longer tail than one who works small ornamental trees, and the adjuster only works with the rope that is actually in it.

Check the length you need, how the ends are finished (a spliced eye, a sewn eye, or a plain tail), and that the diameter is approved for your adjuster or hitch. Compare other options in rope lanyards.

Inspect the rope before every climb for cuts, glazing, and core damage, and retire it after any saw contact. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Keep your old lanyard out of service once the new one is set up, and cut it up so nobody grabs it by mistake.

faq.q: Will this lanyard work in my mechanical adjuster?
faq.a: Only if the rope diameter and type are approved by the adjuster's maker. Check both sets of instructions before you assemble the system.

faq.q: Should I add a steel core lanyard for saw work?
faq.a: Many climbers use a wire-core flipline when cutting near the lanyard. Follow your employer's policy and keep the saw away from any rope lanyard.

name: Handle Insert for Husqvarna 395XP
title: Husqvarna 395XP Handle Insert Replacement Part
meta: Husqvarna 395XP handle insert replacement part. How to confirm the part number, why a worn handle matters on a big saw, and tips for a clean, safe swap.
tagline: A replacement handle insert to keep a 395XP big-bore saw solid in your hands.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP handle insert is a replacement part for the handle assembly on the 395XP, one of the big saws crews still keep for large-diameter felling and bucking. A loose, cracked, or worn handle piece makes a 90-plus cc saw harder to control, so it is worth fixing.
highlights: Replacement part for the Husqvarna 395XP
Restores a firm, secure grip on a heavy saw
Simple swap with basic hand tools
Confirm the part number against your saw
Cheap fix compared with a full handle assembly

body.h: Why handle parts matter on a big saw
p: The 395XP is a heavy saw, and on a long bar it puts a lot of leverage into your hands. Every bit of slop in the handle adds fatigue and makes it harder to hold a clean line through a felling cut or a big round.

Handle inserts and bushings wear, crack, or get chewed up after years of being dropped on the truck bed and dragged through brush. Replacing the insert is a small job that makes an old saw feel tight again.

It is also a good time to look at the antivibration mounts and handle bolts. Worn AV springs make a big saw buzz in your hands, and a handle that moves under load usually means more than one part is tired.
The 395XP was built for many years, so check the illustrated parts list for your serial number and match the part number before ordering. You will find related pieces in power equipment parts.
Work on a cool saw with the chain brake on and the plug wire off. Torque fasteners to spec and check that the throttle, throttle lockout, and chain brake all work properly before starting it back up.
Keep the old part until the new one is fitted so you can compare shape and mounting points side by side.

faq.q: Will this fit a 394XP or 390XP?
faq.a: Some parts are shared across those saws and some are not. Check the part number in Husqvarna's parts list for your model before ordering.

faq.q: Do I need special tools?
faq.a: Usually only the standard screwdriver and Torx bits you already use on the saw. Follow the service manual for the order of disassembly.

name: Husqvarna Worm Drive for T540XP Top-Handle Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna T540XP Worm Drive (Oil Pump Gear)
h1: Husqvarna T540XP Worm Drive (Oil Pump Gear)
meta: Husqvarna T540XP worm drive replacement for the oil pump on the top-handle saw. Signs of a worn worm gear, how to confirm fit, and keeping the bar oiled aloft.
tagline: The small gear that drives the oil pump on a T540XP top-handle saw.
summary: The Husqvarna T540XP worm drive is the small gear that turns the oil pump on the T540XP top-handle chainsaw. When it wears or strips, the bar stops getting oil, and a dry bar and chain on a climbing saw wears out fast and cuts poorly.
highlights: Replacement worm gear for the T540XP oil pump
Restores chain and bar oiling
Inexpensive fix for a dry-running saw
Confirm the part number for your model and serial
Replace with the clutch off for access

body.h: Signs the worm drive is gone
p: Hold the running saw over a stump or a piece of cardboard and rev it. A healthy oiler throws a light line of oil off the nose. If you get nothing, and the tank, oil hole, and bar groove are clean, the worm drive is a likely suspect.

These gears are plastic and wear against the clutch drum. Running a dry tank, a gummed-up pump, or a drum that has been on too long all speed up the wear. A top-handle saw that works aloft all day needs reliable oiling more than most.

The worm drive sits behind the clutch, so you will need a clutch tool and a piston stop. Check the gear, the pump, and the drum while you are in there. More T540XP and other saw parts are in power equipment parts.
Work on a cool saw with the plug wire off, and confirm the oiler is working before the saw goes back up the tree. Top-handle saws are for trained climbers working from a secure position.

If the new gear does not fix the oiling, look at the pump itself, the oil pickup and filter in the tank, and the oil line for cracks. Adjustable pumps should be set to give enough oil for the bar length you run.

faq.q: Does the T536LiXP use the same part?
faq.a: No. The battery saw uses a different drive. This gear is for the gas T540XP; confirm by part number.

faq.q: Should I replace the clutch drum at the same time?
faq.a: If the drum's drive tabs are worn or the rim is grooved, yes. A worn drum can wear the new worm drive faster.

name: Teufelberger tachyon Pink Ash Climbing Rope
title: Teufelberger tachyon Pink Ash Climbing Rope
h1: Teufelberger tachyon Pink Ash Climbing Rope
meta: Teufelberger tachyon pink ash climbing rope: a light, low-stretch 11.5 mm line for SRT and MRS tree climbing. How it handles, hitch fit, and care tips.
tagline: A light 11.5 mm climbing line in a pink and ash color for SRT and MRS work.
summary: Teufelberger tachyon pink ash is the tachyon climbing rope in a pink and ash color, an 11.5 mm line built to be light and low stretch for both SRT and MRS tree climbing. It is a popular choice for climbers who want a smaller, easy-handling rope that still runs well in mechanical devices and friction hitches.
highlights: Teufelberger tachyon in a pink and ash color
About 11.5 mm diameter
Low stretch for efficient SRT ascents
Runs well in common mechanical devices
Firm cover that holds its shape
Easy to spot in the canopy

p: tachyon sits at the light end of arborist climbing lines. At 11.5 mm it is noticeably lighter on a long access line than a 13 mm rope, and its low stretch means less bounce when you are ascending on a single rope. It still has enough body to tend well through a hitch or a micro pulley.
The pink and ash pattern stands out against bark and leaves, which helps a ground worker follow your line and makes it easy to pick your rope out of a pile on a multi-climber job.
Fresh rope will feel a bit firm and slick for the first few climbs. Most climbers find it settles in quickly, but give your hitch a few test runs before trusting your setup up high.

Before you load it, confirm your mechanical device and hitch cord are approved for an 11.5 mm rope, and test the hitch low to the ground. Browse more 24-strand climbing ropes if you want a different diameter.

Keep it in a rope bag, out of the sun and away from saw fuel and bar oil. Inspect the full length often for cuts, glazing, and core damage, and log its use. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.

faq.q: Is tachyon pink ash different from other tachyon colors?
faq.a: The color changes, not the rope. Pick the color that you and your crew can tell apart easily on site.

faq.q: Can I use tachyon for SRT with a Rope Wrench?
faq.a: Many climbers do, but check the device maker's approved rope list and your hitch setup before climbing on it.

name: LockJack Sport Replacement Parts
title: LockJack Sport Replacement Parts
meta: LockJack Sport replacement parts to keep an ISC LockJack Sport running on MRS climbs. What wears, how to match the part, and when to retire the device.
tagline: Factory replacement parts for keeping a LockJack Sport in service.
summary: LockJack Sport replacement parts let you swap out worn components on the LockJack Sport, a mechanical friction device used for moving rope (MRS) tree climbing. Only use the maker's own parts for the specific component that needs replacing.
highlights: Replacement parts for the LockJack Sport
Swap worn components instead of the whole device
Use only the maker's parts on life-support gear
Match the part to your device version
Install per the manufacturer's instructions

body.h: What wears on a mechanical device
p: A mechanical friction device works hard. Rope runs through it all day, grit gets in, and the attachment points rub against connectors. Some components are designed to be replaced when they wear, while others mean the device itself should be retired.
Check your manual to see which parts are user-replaceable. If a part is not listed as replaceable, or you see cracks, deformation, or sharp edges in the body, retire the device.
Keep the device clean. Rinse grit out with fresh water when it gets dirty, let it dry fully, and follow the maker's guidance on lubrication. A device that sticks or drags is telling you something.
Confirm which part you need and that it matches your device version before ordering. Compare other MRS climbing devices if your unit is due for retirement.

Install parts exactly as the instructions show, check that everything moves freely and locks as designed, and test the system low and slow before climbing. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
When in doubt about a part or a symptom, contact the manufacturer before climbing on it again. Write down when you replaced parts in your gear log so you can track the device's history.

faq.q: Can I use parts from another device on my LockJack Sport?
faq.a: No. Only use parts the manufacturer specifies for this device. Mixing parts on life-support equipment is not safe.

faq.q: How do I know if I should retire the device instead?
faq.a: If the body or any non-replaceable part is cracked, bent, grooved, or worn past the maker's limits, retire it.

name: DMM Nomad Replacement Lanyard
title: DMM Nomad Replacement Lanyard
meta: DMM Nomad replacement lanyard to rebuild a worn DMM Nomad lanyard kit with fresh rope. How to match length, what to inspect, and when to replace the whole kit.
tagline: A replacement rope lanyard for the DMM Nomad lanyard kit.
summary: The DMM Nomad replacement lanyard is the rope section for the DMM Nomad lanyard kit, so you can put fresh rope in service without replacing the adjuster and hardware. Lanyard rope wears much faster than the metal parts around it.
highlights: Replacement rope for the DMM Nomad lanyard kit
Keeps your existing hardware in service
Fresh rope after abrasion or saw contact
Check length before ordering
Assemble per DMM's instructions

p: A positioning lanyard gets wrapped around rough bark, run through an adjuster all day, and it lives close to the saw. The rope is the part that suffers. When the cover is fuzzy, glazed, or cut, the rope has to go, but the hardware is often fine.
Buying the replacement lanyard rope keeps the setup you know on your saddle. It also makes it easier to keep a spare in the truck so damage does not end the day.
When you rebuild, look at how the lanyard has been wearing. If the damage is always in the same spot, it may point to how you are wrapping the stem or where the saw is sitting while you cut.
Confirm the length and end terminations match your kit before ordering, and inspect the adjuster and connectors when you swap the rope. Other options are in lanyard kits.

Inspect the lanyard before every climb and retire it after any saw contact or shock load. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Cut up and discard the old lanyard rope so it does not drift back into somebody's gear bag. Write the date of the swap in your gear log.

faq.q: Can I use a different rope in the Nomad kit?
faq.a: Use the rope DMM specifies for the kit. Other ropes may not grip or release correctly in the adjuster.

faq.q: Should I replace the hardware too?
faq.a: Only if inspection shows wear, sharp edges, cracks, or a gate that does not close and lock fully.

name: Husqvarna 550XP Toy Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 550XP Toy Chainsaw for Kids
meta: Husqvarna 550XP toy chainsaw for kids who want to work like the crew. Battery sounds and a plastic chain, with no real cutting parts. Gift and care notes.
tagline: A kid-size, battery-powered toy version of the Husqvarna 550XP.
summary: The Husqvarna 550XP toy chainsaw is a kid-size plastic version of the saw with sounds and a moving plastic chain, so the next generation of tree workers can buck pretend logs in the yard. It has no cutting parts and runs on small batteries.
highlights: Toy modeled on the Husqvarna 550XP
Plastic chain that moves, no cutting parts
Engine sounds on the trigger
Runs on small household batteries
A good gift for a climber's kids

body.h: A toy for the crew's kids
p: Kids who watch a parent head out to work in chaps and a helmet want to do the same thing. This toy looks like the 550XP that a lot of crews run on the ground, with orange and gray colors and a trigger that makes it rattle and rev.

The chain is plastic and the toy has no blade or teeth, so it is safe for play. It is a good way to start talking about saw safety early: helmet on, two hands on the saw, and nobody stands in front of it.
It also makes a fun prop for a kid who wants to dress up in a little helmet and safety glasses, and it is a nice nod to the saws that put food on the table.
Check the age recommendation on the packaging and keep spare batteries on hand. If you are shopping for the real thing, see our chainsaws for working saws.
Keep the toy away from the real saws in the shop, and make sure kids understand that real chainsaws are tools for trained adults only.
Wipe it down with a damp cloth when it gets muddy, and take the batteries out if it is going to sit in a toy box for a while so they do not leak.

faq.q: Does the toy chainsaw cut anything?
faq.a: No. The chain is plastic and has no cutting edges.

faq.q: Does it need batteries?
faq.a: Yes. Check the package for the battery size and whether batteries are included.

name: Husqvarna 36" Bar 3/8 x .063
title: Husqvarna 36 Inch Bar, 3/8 Pitch x .063 Gauge
meta: Husqvarna 36 inch bar in 3/8 pitch and .063 gauge for big saws like the 395XP and 3120XP. Saw fit, matching chain, and handling tips for big-wood felling.
tagline: A 36 inch, 3/8 pitch, .063 gauge bar for big Husqvarna saws on large wood.
summary: This Husqvarna 36 inch bar runs 3/8 pitch, .063 gauge chain and is meant for the big-displacement Husqvarna saws used to fell and buck large trees. It is a specialty length you reach for when a removal leaves you with wood a 24 or 28 inch bar cannot get through.
highlights: 36 inch cutting length
3/8 pitch, .063 gauge
For large Husqvarna saws with enough power to pull it
Built for big-diameter felling and bucking
Pair with a matching 3/8 .063 chain

body.h: When you need a 36 inch bar
p: Most removals never need more than a 20 to 28 inch bar. Then you get a big oak or a cottonwood with a butt too wide to cut from both sides, and a long bar saves a lot of time and repositioning. A 36 inch bar is also handy for slabbing and for big stumps.
It takes a big saw to pull this much chain. Run it on a high-displacement Husqvarna like the 395XP or 3120XP class. A mid-size saw will bog and wear quickly.
Long bars also help when you need to reach across a big log on the ground without climbing on top of it, or when you are working a huge stump down close to grade.
Check your saw's mount and sprocket, and buy a 3/8 pitch, .063 gauge chain with the drive link count that matches this bar. Compare other lengths in chainsaw bars.
A long bar has more kickback zone and more weight out front. Keep a solid stance, wear chaps, a helmet, and eye and ear protection, and only run big saws if you are trained to fell large trees.

Keep the bar rails dressed, flip the bar regularly so it wears evenly, and keep the oil hole and groove clean. A long bar needs plenty of oil, so check that your saw's oiler is set high enough to keep the full length wet.

faq.q: How many drive links does a 36 inch 3/8 bar take?
faq.a: Check the number stamped on the bar tail or Husqvarna's listing for this part, and match the chain to it.

faq.q: Can a 70 cc saw run a 36 inch bar?
faq.a: It will turn it, but slowly and with a lot of strain. Bars this long are best on saws in the 90 cc and up class.

name: DMM Phantom Wiregate Carabiner
title: DMM Phantom Wiregate Carabiner
meta: DMM Phantom wiregate carabiner: a very light non-locking biner for racking tools, slings, and pulleys on your saddle. What it is for and what it must never do.
tagline: A very light non-locking wiregate for racking gear on your saddle.
summary: The DMM Phantom wiregate is one of the lightest full-strength wiregate carabiners around, and in tree work it is a great choice for racking pulleys, slings, and tools. Because it does not lock, it is not for any life-support connection.
highlights: Very light wiregate carabiner
Non-locking, for racking and gear storage
Wire gate resists freezing and gate flutter
Easy to clip with one gloved hand
Never use it as a life-support connector

body.h: Where the Phantom earns its keep
p: Every climber ends up with a saddle covered in pulleys, slings, a handsaw, a spare hitch, and a throw bag. Each of those wants a carabiner, and the weight adds up. A light wiregate like the Phantom shaves grams off every clip point and is easy to open with gloves on.
Wire gates are also less likely to freeze shut in winter and less prone to flutter open when the biner rattles against the saddle.
Many climbers use a handful of light wiregates to build a clean, organized saddle: one for the handsaw, one for spare slings, one for the throw bag, and a couple for pulleys and rigging rings.

body.h: Keep it out of life support
p: Non-locking carabiners are for gear only. Never use one to attach yourself to the climbing system, your lanyard, or any load-bearing part of a rigging system. Locking connectors for those jobs are elsewhere; see non-locking carabiners for more racking options.
Inspect gates for spring and closure, and retire any biner that is dropped from height, cracked, or grooved.
Keep racking carabiners a different color or shape from your life-support connectors so you never grab the wrong one in a hurry. Wash grit out of the gate with fresh water and let it dry.

faq.q: Can I use the Phantom on my lanyard?
faq.a: No. Life-support connections in tree work need self-locking, auto-locking connectors that meet the applicable standard.

faq.q: Why choose a wiregate over a solid gate?
faq.a: A wiregate is lighter, harder to freeze, and less likely to open from vibration.

name: Husqvarna Chainsaw Maintenance Kit for 340, 353, 346XP
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Maintenance Kit for 340, 353, 346XP
meta: Husqvarna chainsaw maintenance kit for the 340, 353, and 346XP. What a tune-up kit covers, how often to service a mid-size saw, and tips to keep it running.
tagline: A tune-up parts kit for Husqvarna's 340, 353, and 346XP mid-size saws.
summary: This Husqvarna chainsaw maintenance kit for the 340, 353, and 346XP bundles common service parts for those mid-size saws, so you can do a full tune-up in one go. Kits like this typically cover the filters and spark plug that wear out with normal use.
highlights: Tune-up kit for 340, 353, and 346XP saws
Typically covers filters and spark plug
One order for a full service
Good for annual or seasonal service
Check the contents list before ordering

body.h: Why a tune-up kit is worth it
p: The 346XP is still a favorite for limbing and bucking because it is light and quick, and lots of 340s and 353s are still working. All three run better and start easier when the air filter, fuel filter, and plug are fresh.
Buying the parts as a kit means you are not hunting part numbers every time. Keep one in the shop and service the saw before it starts acting up rather than after.
Check the spark plug gap and the condition of the fuel line while the saw is apart.
Most crews end up with one or two old mid-size saws as backups. A fresh kit can bring a saw that has sat on the shelf for months back into working shape quickly.

Check the contents list, then replace each part following the service manual. While you are in there, clean the cylinder fins, check the bar oiler, and inspect the sprocket and clutch. More parts are in power equipment parts.
Work on a cool saw with the plug wire off, and test the chain brake and throttle lockout before going back to work.
Use fresh, properly mixed fuel with a good two-stroke oil, and drain the tank if the saw is going to sit for weeks. Stale fuel undoes a tune-up faster than anything.

faq.q: How often should I service my 346XP?
faq.a: Clean the air filter daily in heavy use and do a full tune-up at least once a season, or sooner if the saw is hard to start or down on power.

faq.q: Does this kit fit the 346XP NE?
faq.a: Many parts are shared, but check the contents and part numbers against your exact model and serial number.

name: Petzl ASCENTREE Double-Handled Ascender
title: Petzl ASCENTREE Double-Handled Ascender
meta: Petzl ASCENTREE double-handled ascender for tree climbers. How the two-handle grip helps on long ascents, how it fits an SRT rope walker, and safety checks.
tagline: A double-handled ascender built by Petzl for efficient rope climbing in trees.
summary: The Petzl ASCENTREE is a double-handled ascender designed for tree care, giving you two grip positions so you can push and pull more efficiently on long ascents. It is a common choice for climbers building a fast SRT ascent system.
highlights: Petzl ascender made for tree climbing
Double handle for a better grip with both hands
Built for efficient ascents on long access lines
Pairs with a foot ascender in a rope-walking setup
Use within Petzl's approved rope range

p: On a long SRT ascent, your hands and forearms usually give out before your legs. A double handle lets you change grip, push with both hands, and keep the device square on the rope, which smooths out the stroke and saves energy.
The ASCENTREE is often run as the upper device in a rope-walking or frog-style system, with a foot ascender below. That setup puts most of the work in your legs and gets you into the canopy quickly.

Because it is built for tree work, the ASCENTREE is meant to sit well in a climber's system rather than a caver's or rope-access setup. Many climbers like it for long access climbs on big trees where a single handle wears their grip out.

Check Petzl's instructions for compatible rope diameters and approved configurations, and keep the device connected to your saddle with a suitable tether. Compare other options in ascent and descent gear.

An ascender is not a descent device. Have your descent and changeover worked out before you leave the ground, practice low, and inspect the cams for wear and debris. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Keep the cams clean of sap and grit, and check the teeth for wear. A worn cam can slip on a muddy or icy rope.

faq.q: Can I descend on the ASCENTREE?
faq.a: No. It is for ascending. Change over to an approved descent device or friction system to come down.

faq.q: What rope diameter does it take?
faq.a: Check Petzl's current technical notice for the approved rope range and configurations before using it with your rope.

name: Teufelberger tachyon Ash Climbing Rope
title: Teufelberger tachyon Ash Climbing Rope, 11.5 mm
meta: Teufelberger tachyon climbing rope in ash: a light 11.5 mm line for SRT and MRS tree climbing. How it feels in hitches and devices, plus care and inspection.
tagline: Teufelberger's light 11.5 mm climbing line in a subdued ash color.
summary: Teufelberger tachyon is a light, low-stretch 11.5 mm climbing rope, and the ash color gives it a more subdued look than the brighter versions. Climbers pick tachyon when they want a smaller line that saves weight on long climbs and still works with common SRT devices and hitches.
highlights: Teufelberger tachyon in ash
About 11.5 mm diameter
Low stretch for efficient SRT
Light to carry and throw in a bag
Firm cover that runs smoothly through devices

body.h: A light line for everyday climbing
p: Rope weight adds up on big trees, especially when you are carrying a long access line plus a second rope for a redirect or rescue. tachyon's 11.5 mm diameter cuts weight compared with 13 mm lines while still feeling solid in the hand.

Low stretch helps on SRT, where every inch of bounce is wasted effort. It tends nicely through a hitch-climber pulley and runs well in many mechanical devices, which makes it a versatile all-day line.
The ash color is subtle and looks clean in the canopy, and it is easy to pair with a brighter line if you climb with two ropes and want to tell them apart at a glance.
Confirm every device and hitch in your system is approved for 11.5 mm rope, and fine-tune your hitch on the ground first. Compare other 24-strand climbing ropes if you want a thicker line.

Store it in a rope bag away from sun, fuel, and oil. Inspect the whole length for cuts, glazing, and core damage, and retire it per Teufelberger's guidance. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.

faq.q: Is 11.5 mm too thin for MRS climbing?
faq.a: Many climbers use it for MRS, but your hitch cord and devices must be matched to the diameter. Test thoroughly near the ground.

faq.q: How long should I buy?
faq.a: Buy enough to reach your highest tie-in and back to the ground with extra. Most climbers carry 150 ft or more.

name: Husqvarna Screw for Chain Tensioner for 395XP
title: Husqvarna 395XP Chain Tensioner Screw
meta: Husqvarna 395XP chain tensioner screw replacement. Signs of a stripped tensioner, how to confirm the part number, and keeping chain tension right on a big saw.
tagline: A replacement chain tensioner screw for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP chain tensioner screw replaces the adjusting screw that moves the bar to set chain tension. When the threads strip or the screw bends, you cannot hold proper tension, which is a problem on a saw running a long bar.
highlights: Replacement tensioner screw for the 395XP
Restores reliable chain adjustment
Cheap fix for a stripped tensioner
Confirm part number by serial
Quick swap with the bar off

p: A loose chain can jump the bar, and a chain that is too tight wears the bar and sprocket fast. The tensioner screw is the small part that lets you set it right. If turning it does nothing, or the bar walks loose during a cut, the screw or tensioner nut may be stripped.
On a big saw like the 395XP running a long bar, holding tension is even more important, because a thrown chain does real damage.

Big saws vibrate a lot, and over time the tensioner threads can wear, especially if the bar nuts are not tightened fully before cutting. Overtightening the screw against a stuck bar can also strip it.

Pull the side cover and bar, inspect the tensioner screw and the pin that rides in the bar, and replace worn parts together. Match part numbers in Husqvarna's parts list. Related parts are in power equipment parts.
Work on a cool saw with the chain brake on. Set tension so the chain pulls freely by hand but does not sag from the bottom of the bar, and recheck after the first few cuts.
Tighten bar nuts firmly after setting tension, and do not crank the screw if the bar will not move. Loosen the nuts first, then adjust.

faq.q: Should I replace the tensioner pin too?
faq.a: If the pin or nut is worn or the threads are damaged, yes. They wear as a set.

faq.q: How do I know the screw is stripped?
faq.a: If the screw turns but the bar does not move, or tension slips during cutting, check the threads.

name: Carburetor for Husqvarna 562XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 562XP Mark II Carburetor Replacement
meta: Replacement 562XP Mark II carburetor for the Husqvarna pro saw. When a carb swap makes sense, how to confirm the part, and why AutoTune needs careful setup.
tagline: A replacement carburetor for the Husqvarna 562XP Mark II.
summary: This 562XP Mark II carburetor replaces the carb on Husqvarna's 60 cc class pro saw. When cleaning, filters, and fuel lines do not fix a hard-starting or surging saw, a new carb is often the next step.
highlights: Replacement carburetor for the 562XP Mark II
Fixes stubborn fuel delivery problems
Check part number by model and serial
Pair with new fuel filter and lines
Run the saw in after install

p: Most running problems come from stale fuel, a clogged fuel filter, a cracked fuel line, a dirty air filter, or a blocked tank vent. Check those first. If the saw still will not idle, bogs, or surges after cleaning, the carb diaphragms or metering parts may be done.
The 562XP is an AutoTune saw, so the electronics adjust the mixture. That means a carb fault often shows up as erratic running that cleaning will not fix.

A carb on a 60 cc pro saw takes a lot of vibration and heat, and ethanol fuel left in the tank for weeks can eat diaphragms. If the saw has sat a long time, plan on a fuel system refresh at the same time.
Confirm the part number for your saw and serial, and replace the fuel filter and impulse line if they are old. More 562XP parts are in power equipment parts.
After installation, follow Husqvarna's procedure so the AutoTune system can learn the new carb. Work on a cool saw, check for fuel leaks, and verify the chain does not turn at idle.
Drain fuel before storing the saw and use fresh, properly mixed fuel. Ethanol-free or premixed fuel helps keep a new carb clean.

faq.q: Can I adjust the carb on a 562XP?
faq.a: AutoTune saws do not use manual high and low screws like older saws. Follow Husqvarna's service steps after installing a new carb.

faq.q: Will this fit the original 562XP?
faq.a: Check the part number. The Mark II and earlier models may use different parts.

name: Standard Rigging Kit
title: Standard Tree Rigging Kit for Removals
meta: Standard tree rigging kit with the basic gear for lowering limbs and wood on removals. What a starter kit covers, how to size it, and safe rigging habits.
tagline: A starter set of rigging gear for lowering wood on everyday removals.
summary: This standard tree rigging kit pulls together the core gear a crew needs to start lowering wood on removals, so you are not piecing the system together one part at a time. Check the included items against the size of the wood you plan to rig.
highlights: Starter rigging setup for everyday removals
Gear chosen to work together
Good for crews moving into rigging
Check contents and ratings before ordering
Use within the lowest-rated component

body.h: What a rigging kit is for
p: Rigging is how you take a tree down in pieces over a house, a fence, or a garden. A basic system has a rigging point in the tree, a rigging line, slings to choke the piece and set the block, and a way for the ground worker to control friction as the piece comes down.
A kit takes the guesswork out of matching those parts and gives a crew a consistent setup they can learn on.

Rigging is also where a lot of gear gets damaged and a lot of injuries happen. Having gear that is sized together and kept together in one bag makes it easier to inspect and harder to grab the wrong piece.
Check the listed contents and the rated strength of each part, and keep loads well inside the weakest link. Big wood needs bigger gear; see rigging kits for heavier setups.

Inspect slings, rope, and hardware before every job. Rigging forces climb fast with dynamic loads, so let pieces run, keep the drop zone clear, and make sure everyone on the crew is trained in ANSI Z133 rigging practice.
Store rigging gear dry, out of the sun, and away from saw fuel and bar oil. Log the big loads and retire any gear that has seen a shock load or shows damage.

faq.q: Is this kit enough for large removals?
faq.a: A standard kit is for light to moderate rigging. Large wood needs heavier blocks, rope, slings, and a proper lowering device.

faq.q: Can I use climbing rope for rigging?
faq.a: No. Keep rigging and climbing gear separate. Rigging gear sees loads and abrasion climbing lines are not built for.

name: Kask SC2 Yellow Ear Defenders (Fits Super Plasma and Zenith)
title: Kask SC2 Ear Defenders, Yellow, Super Plasma & Zenith
meta: Kask SC2 ear defenders in yellow that clip onto Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets. Fit, how to check protection, and why muffs belong on every saw job.
tagline: Helmet-mounted yellow earmuffs for Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets.
summary: The Kask SC2 ear defenders are helmet-mounted earmuffs that clip into Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets, giving you hearing protection that swings up when you need to talk. Yellow cups match yellow helmets and make you easy to see.
highlights: Helmet-mounted earmuffs from Kask
Fits Super Plasma and Zenith helmets
Swing up for conversation, down for saw work
Yellow cups for visibility
Replaceable pads and liners
specs: Kask Super Plasma and Zenith helmets

p: Saws, chippers, and stump grinders are loud enough to cause hearing loss over a career. Helmet-mounted muffs are always there when you need them, and they flip up when the saw shuts off so you can talk to the crew.
The SC2 is built to clip into Kask's helmet slots, so it sits right without adapters. Check that your helmet is a compatible model before ordering.
Helmet-mounted muffs also stay with the helmet in the truck, so nobody shows up to the chipper without hearing protection because they left their muffs at home.
The SC2 is meant to integrate with the helmet's other accessories, so you can run a visor and muffs together and keep your eyes and ears covered at the same time.

Check that the cups seal fully around your ears; long hair, glasses arms, and hats under the helmet can break the seal. Replace ear pads when they harden or crack. See other hearing protection options too.
Check the rated noise reduction on the product listing and match it to your exposure. Many crews also wear plugs under muffs for chipper and grinder work.
Muffs that are cracked, crushed, or no longer clamp firmly should be replaced. Check that the arms still hold position up and down.
Wipe the cups clean, and keep them out of the sun on the truck dash, which can harden the seals faster.

faq.q: Will the SC2 fit a Kask Plasma Work helmet?
faq.a: It is listed for Super Plasma and Zenith. Check Kask's compatibility list for other helmets.

faq.q: Can I replace the ear pads?
faq.a: Yes, hygiene kits with new pads and foam are available. Replace them when they lose their seal.

name: CAMP Turbofoot Evo Foot Ascender
title: CAMP Turbofoot Evo Foot Ascender
meta: CAMP Turbofoot Evo foot ascender for SRT tree climbers who want to rope walk. How it fits your boot, pairs with a hand ascender, and where it fits in a system.
tagline: A boot-mounted foot ascender that turns your legs into the engine of an SRT ascent.
summary: The CAMP Turbofoot Evo is a foot ascender that straps to your boot and grabs the rope as you step, so your legs do most of the work on an SRT ascent. It is a popular way for tree climbers to add a step to a rope-walking or frog system.
highlights: Boot-mounted foot ascender from CAMP
Lets your legs do the work on SRT
Pairs with a hand or chest ascender
Tends the rope as you climb
Quick to strap on and remove

body.h: Why climbers add a foot ascender
p: Legs are much stronger than arms. A foot ascender lets you stand up on the rope with each step instead of pulling yourself up hand over hand, which makes long access climbs much less tiring.
It also helps tend the rope below you as you climb, so the system runs cleaner. Most climbers pair it with a handled ascender above and a hitch or device on the saddle.
Many climbers find a foot ascender changes how far they can climb in a day, especially on tall trees or when they are going up and down several times for big pruning jobs.
Strap it to your boot so it sits snug, and practice stepping close to the ground until your rhythm is smooth. See more foot ascenders and foot loops.

A foot ascender is a climbing aid, not a backup. Your primary life-support connection must remain on your saddle. Check CAMP's instructions for rope range and inspect the cam and straps often. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Keep the cam teeth clean of mud and sap, and check the straps and buckles for wear and fraying.

faq.q: Is the Turbofoot Evo for the left or right foot?
faq.a: Check the listing. Foot ascenders are often sold by side, so order the one that fits your setup.

faq.q: Can I use it on MRS?
faq.a: It is meant for ascending on a fixed rope in an SRT system.

name: DMM Kinisi Replacement Rope Bridge
title: DMM Kinisi Replacement Rope Bridge
meta: DMM Kinisi replacement rope bridge for the Kinisi tree saddle. When to replace a worn bridge, how to match the right length, and what to check after fitting.
tagline: A replacement rope bridge for the DMM Kinisi tree climbing saddle.
summary: The DMM Kinisi replacement rope bridge lets you put a fresh bridge on a DMM Kinisi saddle instead of retiring the harness. The bridge is a wear item, and daily climbers often go through several over the life of a saddle.
highlights: Replacement rope bridge for the DMM Kinisi
Cheaper than a new saddle
Restores the main attachment point
Confirm length before ordering
Install per DMM's instructions

p: The bridge is where your climbing system attaches, and it takes every load. It also gets constant abrasion from the hardware sliding along it. Dirt and sawdust speed up wear.
Replacing the bridge gives a saddle a fresh main attachment for little cost. Keep a spare in the truck so a bad inspection does not end the day.
A worn bridge also changes how the saddle rides and where your hardware sits, so climbers often notice a fresh bridge right away.
The Kinisi is designed so the bridge can be swapped without sending the saddle back. That makes it easy to keep a saddle in daily service and a fresh bridge on it.
Check which length you have and want before ordering. A shorter or longer bridge changes how the saddle rides. Other bridges are in saddle parts and shoulder harnesses.

Fit it exactly as DMM's instructions show, and hang-test it low. Inspect for cuts, fuzz, glazing, or stiff areas before each climb. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Keep the old bridge out of service and cut it up so it is not reused by mistake, and note the swap in your gear log.

faq.q: Can I tie my own bridge from climbing rope?
faq.a: Use the bridge DMM specifies. A homemade bridge may not meet the saddle's certification.

faq.q: How do I know it is time to replace it?
faq.a: Replace it when inspection shows cuts, heavy wear, glazing, or stiff spots, or per DMM's guidance.

name: Premium Baltic Birch Outrigger Pads
title: Premium Baltic Birch Outrigger Pads
meta: Baltic birch outrigger pads for bucket trucks, cranes, and lifts. How plywood pads spread load on soft ground, sizing for your rig, and care to make them last.
tagline: Laminated Baltic birch pads to spread outrigger loads on soft ground.
summary: These premium Baltic birch outrigger pads spread the load from a bucket truck or lift outrigger over a larger footprint so the rig stays level and stable on lawns and soft ground. Baltic birch plywood is dense and strong, with many thin plies.
highlights: Laminated Baltic birch plywood
Spreads outrigger load on soft ground
Protects lawns and driveways
Easy to carry and stack
Cheaper than many composite pads

p: A bucket truck outrigger puts a lot of weight on a small foot. On turf, wet ground, or soft asphalt, that foot can sink, and a sinking outrigger can tip the truck. Pads spread the load over a larger area and protect the customer's lawn and driveway.
Baltic birch plywood has many thin, even plies with few voids, which makes it stronger and longer lasting than common plywood.
Pads also help on asphalt on hot days, when outrigger feet can sink in or leave marks, and on pavers or concrete that could crack under a point load.
Wood pads are also easy to cut to fit, quick to stack on the truck, and simple to repair or replace when they get chewed up.
Size the pad to your outrigger foot and the ground you work on, and follow your truck's manual for pad requirements. More gear is in bucket truck accessories.
Set pads on level ground, center the foot, and check for sinking during the job. Store pads dry and replace any that are cracked, split, or delaminating.
Do not set pads on steep slopes, frozen ground that may thaw, or over voids like buried tanks and culverts. Keep a rope handle or hand hold on each pad to make it easy to pick up and place.

faq.q: Are wood pads as good as plastic?
faq.a: Good plywood pads work well, but they absorb water. Store them dry and inspect them often.

faq.q: What size do I need?
faq.a: Follow your truck maker's guidance; larger pads spread the load more on soft ground.

name: Singing Tree Rope Wrench Slick Pin
title: Singing Tree Rope Wrench Slick Pin
h1: Singing Tree Rope Wrench Slick Pin
meta: Singing Tree Rope Wrench slick pin replacement part for the SRT friction device. When to replace it, how to match your Rope Wrench version, and inspection tips.
tagline: A replacement slick pin for the Singing Tree Rope Wrench.
summary: The Singing Tree Rope Wrench slick pin is a replacement part for the Rope Wrench, the SRS friction device used with a hitch for single-rope tree climbing. Worn parts on a life-support device should be replaced only with the maker's own parts.
highlights: Replacement part for the Singing Tree Rope Wrench
Use only factory parts on life-support gear
Confirm compatibility with your Rope Wrench version
Simple swap when worn
Install per manufacturer instructions

body.h: Keeping a Rope Wrench in service
p: The Rope Wrench adds friction to a hitch in an SRS system, letting you climb and descend on a single rope. Its parts take constant rope wear and grit, and some parts are designed to be replaced when they wear.
Replacing a worn pin with the maker's own part is cheaper than replacing the whole device and keeps it running the way it was designed.
Like any part of an SRS system, the pin and the parts it connects take load on every descent, so wear there is a real concern rather than a cosmetic one.
Check which Rope Wrench version you have and confirm this part is right for it. More devices are in SRS climbing devices.

Install it as the instructions show, check that all parts are secure, and test low. Retire the device if the body is cracked, grooved, or worn past limits. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Keep the device clean of sap and grit, and check that the tether, spring, and connectors are in good shape. Log the swap in your gear records.

faq.q: Can I use a hardware-store pin?
faq.a: No. Use only the manufacturer's part on life-support equipment.

faq.q: How do I know the pin is worn?
faq.a: Look for grooves, wear, bending, or a loose fit, and replace it per the instructions.

name: 900 Series Compatible Stump Grinding Teeth
title: 900 Series Compatible Stump Grinding Teeth
meta: 900 series compatible stump grinding teeth for grinders that take 900 style pockets. How to spot dull teeth, rotating them, and safety tips for grinding.
tagline: Replacement carbide teeth for grinders that take 900 series style teeth.
summary: These 900 series compatible stump grinding teeth are replacement teeth for grinders set up for the 900 series pocket style. Sharp teeth cut faster, load the machine less, and leave a cleaner hole.
highlights: Compatible with 900 series tooth pockets
Carbide cutting tip
Replaces worn or broken teeth
Rotate teeth to extend life
Check your wheel layout before ordering

p: Dull or chipped teeth make a grinder bounce, chatter, and work harder. If you see more dust than chips, or the machine struggles in soft wood, look at the teeth. Hitting rocks or metal will chip carbide fast.
Some teeth can be rotated to a fresh edge before you replace them. Check your wheel layout and replace in sets when wear is even.
Keep spare teeth and pocket hardware sorted in the truck, and note how many hours each set lasts so you can plan reorders before a busy week.
Teeth wear faster in sandy or rocky soil. Clean around the stump and remove rocks before grinding to save teeth and keep debris from flying.
Confirm your cutter wheel is set up for 900 series style pockets, and torque bolts to the maker's spec. More grinding gear is in stump grinding.
Shut the machine down and remove the key before changing teeth. Wear eye and face protection, chaps or pants, and keep people well back from the grinding area.
Replace pocket bolts and nuts if they are worn or stretched, and check the wheel for cracks. Keep spare teeth in the truck so a broken one does not end the job.

faq.q: Will these fit my grinder?
faq.a: Only if your cutter wheel uses 900 series style pockets. Check your manual.

faq.q: How often do teeth need replacing?
faq.a: It depends on soil, rocks, and hours. Check them daily.

name: Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester Hitch Cord (by the foot)
title: Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester Hitch Cord
meta: Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester hitch cord, sold by the foot to tie your own friction hitches. How to pick the length, match the rope, and check hitch wear.
tagline: 10 mm polyester hitch cord sold by the foot for tying friction hitches.
summary: This Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester hitch cord is sold by the foot, so you can cut the length you need for friction hitches and prusiks. Polyester handles the heat of a running hitch better than nylon.
highlights: 10 mm polyester hitch cord
Sold by the foot
Good heat resistance for friction hitches
Cut to the length you want
Match diameter to your climbing rope

body.h: Why buy hitch cord by the foot
p: Buying by the foot lets you cut the exact length you need for your hitch. A longer cord gives you more wraps and more grip, while a shorter one is quicker to tend. Climbers often keep a spare length to retie after wear.
Polyester holds up better to heat than nylon, which matters when a hitch is running during a descent.
Buying cord by the foot is also handy when you want to try a different hitch length or tie a second hitch for a backup.

Many climbers like 10 mm polyester for eye-to-eye hitches because it grabs well, runs smoothly, and holds its shape after many descents. It also works for prusiks and backup hitches on rigging and rescue setups.
Match the hitch cord to your climbing rope. A 10 mm cord works on many 11 to 13 mm climbing lines, but test the hitch low. More cords are in tech cordage.

Check hitches before each climb for glazing, stiffness, and cover wear, and retire them early. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.
Store cord out of the sun and away from oil and fuel. Hitch cord wears much faster than climbing rope, so keep spares on hand.

faq.q: How long should I cut my hitch cord?
faq.a: It depends on your hitch and rope. Many climbers start around 30 in and adjust.

faq.q: Can I tie my own eyes?
faq.a: Only if you are trained in the correct knots. Many climbers buy spliced eye-to-eye cords.

name: Husqvarna Air Filter Assembly for 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Air Filter Assembly
h1: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Air Filter Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II air filter assembly to keep dust and chips out of the engine. Cleaning tips, when to replace the filter, and how to check the fit.
tagline: A replacement air filter assembly for the 550XP Mark II.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP Mark II air filter assembly replaces the filter that keeps dust and chips out of the engine on Husqvarna's 50 cc pro saw. A clean filter keeps the saw running strong and protects the piston and cylinder.
highlights: Replacement air filter assembly
For the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
Protects the engine from dust
Easy tool-free swap
Keep a spare in the truck

p: The 550XP Mark II is a favorite for limbing and bucking, and it spends its life in sawdust, chips, and dry, dusty brush piles. The air filter is what stands between that debris and the engine. A clogged filter starves the engine of air and cuts power, and a torn or poorly seated filter lets fine dust into the cylinder, where it wears the piston and rings.
The Mark II also uses AutoTune, which adjusts the fuel mixture as conditions change. A dirty filter makes it work harder to compensate and can make the saw feel sluggish or run hot.
Check the filter daily during heavy use. On a dusty job, that may mean checking it at every fuel stop.

Tap loose debris off or blow it clean with low-pressure air from the inside out so you do not push dirt into the media. Follow Husqvarna's guidance on whether and how to wash the filter. Replace it when it is torn, warped, oil-soaked, or will not come clean. Other service parts are in power equipment parts.

Confirm the part number for your saw and serial before ordering, since the original 550XP and the Mark II use some different parts. When you install it, make sure it seats fully and the cover locks down so no air slips past the edge.
Keep a spare filter in the truck so you can swap a dirty one on the job and clean it back at the shop. Work on a cool saw with the chain brake on.

faq.q: Can I wash the 550XP Mark II air filter?
faq.a: Follow Husqvarna's cleaning guidance for this filter. When it is torn, warped, or will not come clean, replace it.

faq.q: Does it fit the original 550XP?
faq.a: Some parts differ between the original 550XP and the Mark II. Check the part number against your model and serial.

name: Weaver Stratus Saddle
title: Weaver Stratus Saddle for Tree Climbing
meta: Weaver Stratus saddle for tree climbers. How to fit a Weaver saddle, what to check before every climb, and how to set it up for the work you do most.
tagline: A Weaver tree climbing saddle for daily work positioning.
summary: The Weaver Stratus saddle is a tree climbing saddle from Weaver, a long-time name in arborist saddles. Like any saddle, fit and comfort matter most when you hang in it all day.
highlights: Tree climbing saddle from Weaver
For work positioning in the canopy
Adjustable fit
Check Weaver's sizing chart before ordering
Inspect before every climb

p: A climbing saddle is where you spend most of a work day, so fit and comfort matter as much as anything on the spec sheet. A good saddle spreads your weight across the waist and legs, keeps the bridge or attachment points where you can reach them, and carries the tools you need without getting in the way.

Weaver has made tree saddles for a long time, and many climbers like their straightforward, durable designs. Before ordering, check the sizing chart against your waist and leg measurements, and be honest about the clothing you wear in winter. If you can, hang in a saddle before you commit to it and check how the leg loops and waist belt feel when you lean back into your lanyard.
Think about how you climb. An SRT climber, a spur-heavy removal climber, and a pruning climber may want different attachment points and gear storage.
Adjust the saddle per Weaver's instructions and set up your gear loops so the tools you use most are easiest to reach. Compare other models in Weaver saddles.

Inspect webbing, stitching, buckles, D-rings, and the bridge or attachment points before every climb. Look for cuts, burns, chemical stains, worn stitching, and cracked or bent hardware. Keep the saddle clean, dry it away from direct heat, and store it out of the sun.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.

faq.q: How do I size a Weaver saddle?
faq.a: Use Weaver's sizing chart for this model and measure over the clothing you usually climb in.

faq.q: Can parts of the saddle be replaced?
faq.a: Check Weaver's instructions for which parts, if any, are replaceable, and use only Weaver parts.

name: PFERD Chain Saw Sharpening Set
title: PFERD Chainsaw Sharpening Set for Field Filing
meta: PFERD chainsaw sharpening set with files and guides for keeping chain sharp in the field. How to pick a file size, what to check, and good filing habits.
tagline: A field sharpening set for keeping chainsaw chain cutting clean.
summary: The PFERD chainsaw sharpening set puts the files and guides you need to touch up a chain in one kit, so you can keep the saw cutting clean on the job. PFERD is a German maker known for quality files.
highlights: Chainsaw sharpening set from PFERD
Files and guides in one kit
For field touch-ups
Choose the file size for your chain
Quality German files

p: A dull chain makes fine dust instead of thick chips, pulls the saw off line, and makes you lean on the saw to get through the cut. That wears you out, wears the bar and sprocket, and raises the chance of a kickback or a bad cut. Touching up the chain with a file every tank or two in clean wood keeps it cutting the way it should.

A good field sharpening set puts the pieces you need in one place, so you are not hunting for the right file in the truck. Look for a round file sized to your chain, a holder or guide that keeps your angle and depth consistent, and a flat file and depth gauge tool for setting the rakers.
PFERD is a German maker with a long history in files, and its chainsaw files hold their cut well.

body.h: Choosing a size and filing well
p: Check the contents of the set and make sure the round file matches your chain's pitch and the file size its maker calls for. Using the wrong file size changes the shape of the cutter. Other tools are in wrenches and files.

Set the chain brake or lock the bar in a vise, wear gloves, and give each cutter the same number of strokes so they stay the same length. File the rakers lightly after several sharpenings, not every time. If you hit a rock or a nail, take the chain to the shop for a grind instead of trying to file it all back in the field.

faq.q: What file size do I need?
faq.a: Check your chain's packaging or the chain maker's chart. File size depends on the chain pitch and cutter type.

faq.q: How often should I file my chain?
faq.a: Touch it up every tank or two in clean wood, and any time it starts making dust instead of chips.

name: Samson Pro-Master 1/2" Rigging Rope
title: Samson Pro-Master 1/2 in Rigging Rope
meta: Samson Pro-Master 1/2 in rigging rope for lowering limbs and moderate wood. How to size a rigging line, match it to blocks and devices, and inspect it often.
tagline: A 1/2 in rigging line from Samson for everyday lowering.
summary: Samson Pro-Master rigging rope in 1/2 inch is a rigging line for lowering limbs and moderate wood on removals. Half-inch is a common size for pruning and light to moderate rigging.
highlights: Samson rigging rope
1/2 in diameter
For light to moderate rigging
Pair with suitable blocks and devices
Inspect before every job

body.h: Where a 1/2 inch rigging line fits
p: A 1/2 inch rigging line is the everyday size for a lot of crews. It is light enough to throw over a limb, run through a small block, and handle all day, while still being up to lowering limbs and smaller wood on pruning jobs and removals. Bigger wood calls for bigger rope, but a 1/2 inch line covers a lot of the work.

Samson is a long-time name in arborist rope, and Pro-Master is one of its rigging lines. Before you buy, check the published strength, construction, and length options for the rope you are ordering, and make sure they suit the gear and loads in your system.
Keep rigging rope for rigging only. Rigging lines take shock loads, abrasion, and pitch that a climbing line should never see.

Work well under the rated strength of the rope and every other part of the system, and remember that a piece that drops before the rope comes tight puts far more load on everything. Match the rope to your blocks, lowering device, and slings. Compare other options in rigging rope.

Inspect the line before every job for cuts, pulled strands, glazing, flat spots, and hard or stiff sections. Keep it clean, out of the sun, and away from fuel and bar oil, and retire it when damage is found. Make sure everyone on the crew is trained in rigging under ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Is 1/2 in rope enough for big wood?
faq.a: No. Heavy pieces call for larger rope and gear rated for the loads. Use a 1/2 in line for limbs and smaller wood.

faq.q: Can I splice Pro-Master?
faq.a: Check Samson's splicing instructions for this rope's construction, or buy it with a factory splice.

name: DMM Revolver Rig Screw Gate Carabiner
title: DMM Revolver Rig Screw Gate Carabiner
meta: DMM Revolver Rig screw gate carabiner with a built-in pulley wheel for redirects, haul systems, and rigging. How the roller helps and where screw gates fit in.
tagline: A screw gate carabiner with a built-in pulley wheel to cut friction.
summary: The DMM Revolver Rig is a screw gate carabiner with a built-in pulley wheel in the base, cutting rope friction in redirects and haul systems. It is a compact way to add a small pulley without carrying one.
highlights: Screw gate carabiner from DMM
Built-in pulley wheel
Cuts friction in redirects
Compact and light
Handy for haul systems

p: The DMM Revolver line puts a small pulley wheel in the base of a carabiner. Rope running over that wheel sees less friction than it would over a plain carabiner, which makes redirects smoother, saves rope wear, and helps when you are building a small mechanical advantage system to tension a line or haul gear.

The Revolver Rig version uses a screw gate, which is simple, durable, and easy to inspect. Because the wheel is built in, you get some of the benefit of a pulley without carrying a separate one and a second carabiner.
Climbers often use one as a redirect on a long SRT line or for a quick haul system to bring up a saw or a pole tool. In rigging, it can help on light lines where you want rope to run cleanly.

A pulley carabiner is not a substitute for a full rigging block or a proper pulley when the loads are big. Check DMM's ratings for the wheel and the carabiner and stay well inside them. Compare other options in screw gate carabiners.

Screw gates must be screwed fully closed before loading, and many tree care employers require auto-locking connectors for life support. Follow your employer's policy and the applicable standard. Check that the wheel spins freely and that the gate closes and locks fully. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.

faq.q: Can I use a screw gate for life support?
faq.a: Many tree care rules call for auto-locking connectors in life support. Follow your employer's policy and the applicable standard.

faq.q: Does the wheel need care?
faq.a: Rinse grit out with fresh water, let it dry, and check that it spins freely before use.

name: Silky Ibuki 16" (390mm) Curved Saw with Scabbard
title: Silky Ibuki 390mm Curved Hand Saw with Scabbard
h1: Silky Ibuki 16" (390mm) Curved Saw with Scabbard
meta: Silky Ibuki 390mm curved hand saw with scabbard for climbers cutting big limbs. How the long curved blade cuts, carrying it aloft, and blade care tips.
tagline: A long curved Silky hand saw with scabbard for cutting big limbs.
summary: The Silky Ibuki is a 390mm curved hand saw with a scabbard, made for cutting big limbs fast without starting a chainsaw. The long curved blade pulls into the cut and takes big bites.
highlights: 390mm curved blade
Large teeth for fast cuts
Comes with scabbard
Good for climbers and ground work
Replaceable blade

p: The Silky Ibuki is built for cutting big wood by hand. A 390 mm curved blade pulls into the cut on the pull stroke, so you spend less effort pushing the saw and more time cutting. That length handles limbs that would take forever with a short folding saw, and it can save you from starting a saw for a few cuts in a crown.
A hand saw is also quiet and has no fuel, chain, or kickback, which makes it a good choice near homes, in tight crowns, and in delicate pruning where you want precise cuts at the branch collar.
Climbers often carry a big Silky on the saddle as the main pruning tool and leave the top-handle saw for removals.

body.h: Carrying it and caring for it
p: Keep the blade in its scabbard any time it is not in your hand, and clip the scabbard securely to your saddle so it does not swing. A long blade is sharp along its full length, so watch your rope, lanyard, and legs when you are cutting close. More options are in hand saws and scabbards.

Wipe sap off the blade after use and keep it dry to prevent rust. Silky blades are hard to sharpen well, so most climbers swap in a replacement blade when it gets dull or bent. Confirm the replacement blade part fits your handle before ordering.

faq.q: Can I replace the Ibuki blade?
faq.a: Yes. Silky sells replacement blades. Confirm the part matches your saw before ordering.

faq.q: Is the Ibuki good for climbing?
faq.a: Many climbers carry it, but it is a long blade. Keep it in a secure scabbard and be careful around your rope and lanyard.

name: ISC Offset D Supersafe Carabiner with Locking Pin
title: ISC Offset D Supersafe Carabiner, Locking Pin
h1: ISC Offset D Supersafe Carabiner with Locking Pin
meta: ISC Offset D supersafe carabiner with a locking pin for climbers who want an auto-locking connector that resists rollout. Shape, gate action, and inspection.
tagline: An offset D auto-locking carabiner with a locking pin for tree climbing.
summary: The ISC Offset D supersafe carabiner is an auto-locking connector with an extra locking pin that guards against accidental opening. The offset D shape opens wide and loads well.
highlights: Offset D shape
Auto-locking gate
Locking pin for extra security
ISC build quality
Good for saddle attachment

p: In tree work, carabiners rub against bark, ropes, and other hardware all day. A standard auto-locking gate can still be opened by a rope or branch twisting across it in the right direction. The ISC supersafe design adds a locking pin, so the gate needs an extra deliberate action before it opens.

The offset D shape puts the load close to the spine, where the carabiner is strongest, and gives a wide gate opening for clipping a bridge, a rope, or a thick eye. That makes it a good fit for saddle attachment points, lanyards, and other places where you want maximum security.
The trade-off is that it takes a bit more practice to open, especially with gloves or cold hands.

Load the carabiner along its long axis, and do not let it cross-load against the gate. Check the markings and ISC's instructions for ratings and approved uses. Compare other options in auto-locking carabiners.

Before each climb, check that the gate opens smoothly, closes fully, and that the locking pin engages every time. Look for grooves, sharp edges, cracks, and corrosion, and retire the carabiner after a big fall or drop. Rinse grit out with fresh water and dry it well. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it.

faq.q: Is it hard to open with gloves?
faq.a: It takes a little practice. Work the gate on the ground until opening it is second nature.

faq.q: Is it rated for life support?
faq.a: Check the markings and ISC's instructions for ratings and approved uses, and follow your employer's policy.
